Subject: Marketplace procurement checklist and billing model for Redwood inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the overview call yesterday. Our procurement team is starting the intake for marketplace-sourced SaaS and we want to make sure Redwood maps cleanly to Acme's purchase controls and our cloud procurement flows. Can you confirm the following at a high level? We can loop in legal/compliance next.

1) Marketplace channels supported: do you support AWS Marketplace (SaaS monthly metered + private offer), Azure Marketplace (SaaS + managed offer), and GCP Marketplace SaaS? Any differences we should be aware of?

2) Billing entity and invoice model: which legal entity issues invoices when we buy via each marketplace vs a direct private offer? Can you provide an example invoice that includes the marketplace fields we need (PO number, customer billing code, tax id, GL code placeholder)?

3) Private offer and discounts: if we commit to a 12-month committed spend, is a private offer required? How are credits/ refunds handled if usage is lower than committed?

4) Entitlements / seat mapping: for marketplace purchases, how are entitlements provisioned on your side (marketplace entitlements vs direct license keys)?

5) Compliance & DPA: can you provide your SOC 2 report and the standard DPA you request? Any constraints re: data residency, retention, audit rights?

6) Integrations: SSO (SAML/SCIM), firewall IPs, and required metadata for SAML exchanges — what do you need from us to onboard?

7) Timeline: typical turnaround for a private-offer setup and procurement acceptance for an enterprise buyer?

If it helps, I can attach our marketplace intake spreadsheet with the specific fields we need.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our renewal window is mid-April.

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Financial

Elena —

Great questions, thanks. High-level answers below and I attached a short playbook + technical annex that covers most of the marketplace-specific implementation notes. I’ll loop in Compliance/Platform for the deeper legal/technical items once you confirm you want to proceed with a private offer.

1) Channels supported: Redwood supports AWS Marketplace (we offer SaaS metered + private offers), Azure Marketplace (SaaS/managed offers), and GCP Marketplace (SaaS). Differences: AWS private offers support committed pricing and passthrough billing; Azure managed offer options vary by seller type — see annex for a table. GCP supports both direct marketplace SaaS and SaaS with private agreement.

2) Billing entity: For marketplace purchases the marketplace typically issues the invoice to the buyer and remits funds to Redwood Cloud, Inc. (our seller entity). For private offers, we can surface a Redwood-generated invoice if requested — sample invoice attached. Invoices will include PO, tax id, and a buyer reference field (GL code) where available.

3) Private offers: Yes — for committed-term discounted pricing we generally use a private offer (marketplace private offer or vendor-managed contract depending on region). Credits for unused committed spend are handled per the offer terms (we can do monthly true-ups or quarterly credits).

4) Entitlements: We can support both marketplace entitlement propagation (recommended for AWS/Azure) and direct entitlements issued from our licensing service. For enterprise buyers we often map marketplace entitlements to account-level entitlements during onboarding to simplify provisioning.

5) Compliance & DPA: SOC 2 Type II report and our standard DPA are available; we can provide the SOC 2 pack under NDA and a redline-friendly DPA via DocuSign. Data residency options: US-East and EU-West regions; retention and audit rights spelled out in the DPA.

6) Integrations: We support SAML 2.0 & SCIM for user provisioning. IP ranges and firewall rules are in the technical annex. For SAML we need SP metadata and ACS URL from your IdP; we can generate ours on request.

7) Timeline: Private-offer acceptance and seller-side setup typically take 7–12 business days assuming paperwork is standard and procurement signs the offer. For marketplace entitlements + provisioning add ~3 business days.

Attachments: Redwood-Marketplace-Playbook.pdf, AWS_Marketplace_Technical_Annex.docx

If you’d like, we can schedule a short 30-minute session with our Marketplace Ops and Platform SRE to walk the annex and confirm the fields.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Strategic Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the quick summary and the attachments. We reviewed the annex and have a few detailed follow-ups (I captured them in the attached spreadsheet). Key items requiring clarification:

• Invoice sample: we need a sample invoice with the exact field names our AP system expects (Vendor Tax ID, Vendor legal name, Buyer PO number, Buyer billing code/GL, Invoice line item SKU and quantity, Marketplace fees separated). Can you provide?

• Taxes & GST: please confirm Redwood’s tax id(s) and whether marketplace sales collect/remit taxes on Redwood’s behalf in the US.

• Refund/credit process for private offers: example scenarios where monthly committed usage < allocated; how credits are applied and reporting cadence.

• DPA: We need a DPA with explicit audit rights (up to quarterly), data center locations for the tenant, and subprocessor list. Can you also share the most recent SOC2 Type II report or at least a letter confirming continuous coverage?

• Onboarding steps: firewall IPs, SAML metadata exchange template, SCIM user attribute mapping, and the expected lead time for network allowlist and SSO setup.

• Entitlement reconciliation: if we purchase via AWS Marketplace private offer but want to track consumption in our internal billing system, can you provide a metering feed or report (daily/weekly) that maps marketplace tokens to our customer IDs?

• Cancellations & refunds: what's your standard cancellation notice period and refund policy for marketplace-sourced subscriptions?

I attached our Acme_Marketplace_Questions.xlsx with the required fields highlighted. We’re targeting a decision by April 15 so answers by end of next week would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elena

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the spreadsheet — apologies for the delay. Below are concrete answers and attachments for the fields you highlighted. I’ve pulled in the Platform Ops attachments and included a sample invoice as requested.

Invoice & Billing
• Attached: Redwood_Sample_Invoice.pdf — includes fields: Vendor legal name (Redwood Cloud, Inc.), Vendor tax ID (ETA: full tax id on NDA), Buyer PO number, Buyer billing code / GL field, Invoice line SKU, quantity, unit price, marketplace fee line item. For marketplace-billed purchases, the marketplace vendor invoice will include their platform fee; for private offers we can issue a Redwood-generated invoice that mirrors the marketplace fields.
• Taxes: Marketplace purchases often have tax collected by the marketplace; we will confirm Redwood’s tax registrations for US states as part of seller onboarding.

Private Offer / Credits
• Private offers: we recommend private offers for committed discounts. For underutilization we support monthly true-ups with credits applied to subsequent invoices or a quarterly settlement — customer choice documented in the SOW/offer.

Metering & Entitlement Feeds
• We provide a daily metering CSV export (SFTP) or an authenticated API endpoint delivering consumption records mapped to your internal customer ID (we require the mapping during onboarding). See Azure_Seller_Request_Spec.xlsx for the field mapping and sample payload.

DPA & SOC2
• We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. Our standard DPA is available via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/Redwood-DPA-sign/ABC123. The DPA includes audit rights (annual/quarterly negotiable), subprocessor list and data center regions (US-East, US-West, EU-West).

Security & Onboarding
• SSO: SAML 2.0 SP metadata and SCIM attribute map attached in the Azure_Seller_Request_Spec.xlsx. Typical lead time for allowlist + SSO = 3–5 business days after we receive IdP metadata and firewall tickets.
• IP ranges: listed in the technical annex; can be allowlisted per environment (prod vs staging).

Cancellations/Refunds
• Cancellation: Standard marketplace subscriptions follow marketplace cancellation rules. For private offers we specify termination clauses in the SOW — typical notice is 30 days, with refund/credit mechanics defined in the private offer terms.

Timeline
• Private offer + seller acceptance: ~7–12 business days.
• Metering / entitlement reconciliation setup: ~3–5 business days after entitlement config is confirmed.

Attachments included: Azure_Seller_Request_Spec.xlsx, Redwood_Sample_Invoice.pdf

Next steps: If this looks good I’ll share the SOC2 NDA link and the DPA DocuSign envelope. We can also schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with Platform Ops to confirm the SAML attributes and the mapping for metering IDs.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Platform & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
